name: Potato slices / juice

lead: Raw potato slices or grated-potato juice are a folk remedy placed under the eyes for dark circles and puffiness. Proponents describe potato as a natural lightener and, when chilled, a cooling compress, aiming for a lighter, less puffy under-eye.

Believers say compounds in raw potato lighten pigment, and cold slices may soothe the area. No published study was found testing potato for this purpose, and reference articles on dark circles do not list it among evaluated treatments.

paras: People lay thin chilled slices on closed eyes for 10 to 20 minutes, or dab fresh grated-potato juice under the eyes and rinse it off, usually as an occasional home treatment.

No safety data were found for this use. Raw potatoes contain glycoalkaloids such as solanine and chaconine, which rise in green or damaged tubers; whether skin application matters has not been studied. Contact irritation is possible with any raw plant material.

angle.text: Home-remedy communities apply raw potato slices or juice under the eyes as a folk lightener for dark circles and puffiness. The idea is that compounds in raw potato lighten pigment while the cold slice soothes swelling. No studies of it for dark circles were found.

lead: Potato slices or juice is a folk remedy in which thin slices of raw potato, or grated or juiced potato, are placed on the skin under the eyes to lighten dark circles and reduce puffiness. It circulates in home-remedy and beauty communities as a cheap, kitchen-based way to look more rested.

Proponents describe two effects. One is a cooling compress effect, strongest when the slices are chilled, which they say calms morning puffiness. The other is a natural lightening effect on the pigment beneath the eyes, which they attribute to the potato itself.

Dermatology references list the causes of under-eye darkness as thin eyelid skin and underlying anatomy, allergy and rubbing, pigmentation, fatigue, age and sun exposure, and name hydroquinone, caffeine and vitamin C creams, lasers, fillers and fat transfer among treatments; potato is not among the treatments they describe [1]. No clinical study of potato applied to the periorbital area has been published.
infobox: Raw slices, grated pulp or juice

paras: The remedy is applied as slices laid over closed eyes for a period of time, or as grated pulp or juice dabbed on the skin. Cold storage before use is common and links it to the cold compress practice.

Practitioners say the slices or juice lighten pigment and reduce swelling. Under-eye puffiness and darkness have many recognised causes, including allergy, fatigue, anatomy and pigmentation, so people report varied results depending on the cause [1].

Raw potatoes contain glycoalkaloids, chiefly solanine and chaconine. Levels are highest in the skin, rise when tubers are exposed to light and turn green, and are higher in damaged or aged tubers; properly grown and stored tubers contain only small amounts [2].

No study has examined how potato affects eyelid skin. Because it is a raw plant material applied near the eyes, people with sensitive skin or allergy tendencies may react, and glycoalkaloid content is greater in green or sprouting potatoes [2].
